prov_ham_nguyet.name: Hàm Nguyệt
prov_ham_nguyet.lore: Birch and pine shore along the western end of Hạo Nguyệt Hồ, where the long lake is calmest. Its people fish, tend pearl beds and cut birch for Hàm Nguyệt Trang, which rules the shore for Tùng Đào Cung. Pearls and spirit fish are its wealth, and every fisher here knows the old saying that the moon in the lake is easier to catch than the one in the sky.

prov_p55.name: Quy Điểu
prov_p55.lore: Low pine forest running down to the shore around Quy Điểu Trấn, loud with birds every autumn. Townsfolk and woodsmen live by the pearl market, fowling and timber. The winter ice market draws pearl buyers from all three of Tùng Đào's lands.

prov_p95.name: Tuyết Lộc
prov_p95.lore: A cold strip of forest, lichen tundra and frozen bog on the snowy north shore, grazed by the reindeer of Tuyết Lộc Thôn. Herders trade hides and antler for salt with the Băng Tâm fishers who share this shore since the Long Lake War. Snow leopards still come down from the bogs in hard winters.

prov_p96.name: Hàn Yên
prov_p96.lore: A small stretch of pine and birch on the shore around Hàn Yên Thôn, where winter smoke hangs frozen over the chimneys. Its people fish through the ice and cut firewood. The village bell still calls the children in before dusk, a habit kept since the snow-leopard hunt of 610.

prov_p97.name: Noãn Ốc
prov_p97.lore: A sheltered shore of pine around the domed stone houses of Noãn Ốc Thôn and its hot spring. Its people fish and rent bath hours to old cultivators who come to soak their bones each winter. Tùng Đào counts the hamlet among the warmest places of its cold north.

prov_r1_1.name: Bắc Đài Nguyên
prov_r1_1.lore: Flat lichen tundra on the far northern shore, frozen most of the year and broken only by stands of stunted larch. No one lives here; reindeer herders cross it in summer and leave before the first snow. White bears den along its shore, and Tùng Đào sends no patrols past the larches.

prov_r1_10.name: Hàn Sam Lâm
prov_r1_10.lore: Dark fir forest thinning into tundra and bog, with no road and no village. Trappers enter it only in winter, when the bogs freeze and the wolf packs are easier to hear. Its timber is too far from any water to be worth the cutting.

prov_r1_11.name: Tùng Chi
prov_r1_11.lore: Rolling inland pine forest whose people tap resin from the old trees and boil it into pitch for the lake boats. A quiet spirit vein of wood qi runs under its oldest roots. The empty fur town in its hills is a reminder of what happens when a forest is trapped bare.

prov_r1_12.name: Ngư Đăng
prov_r1_12.lore: Forest and reed swamp along the shore, its people fishing by lantern light on autumn nights. They sell smoked fish to Quy Điểu Trấn and pay their dues to Tùng Đào in pitch and dried fish. Great owls hunt the swamp edge and the villagers will not go into it after dark.

prov_r1_13.name: Tùng Than
prov_r1_13.lore: Pine forest running down to a long pale beach at the western end of the region. Its people fish, build small boats and gather pine pitch to caulk them. The forest behind the beach is thick enough that Tùng Đào's surveyors once counted its trees and gave up.

prov_r1_14.name: Hồi Lưu
prov_r1_14.lore: Low forest where a river turns back on itself before it meets the shore, leaving still backwaters full of eels. Its people set eel traps and strip birch bark. They pay Hàm Nguyệt Trang in smoked eel each autumn.

prov_r1_15.name: Thán Diêu
prov_r1_15.lore: Unbroken inland forest of larch and pine, smoky with charcoal kilns. Its burners make charcoal from fallen and dead wood only, by Tùng Đào's rule, and sell it to the lake towns for the winter. The kiln smoke can be seen for a day's walk.

prov_r1_16.name: Nguyệt Tân
prov_r1_16.lore: Forest along the river where it runs down toward the long lake, with a small side lake of its own. Nguyệt Tân Trấn ferries timber, pitch and pearls between the lake and the inland villages. It is the busiest crossing in Lãnh Nguyệt Lâm outside the pearl towns.

prov_r1_17.name: Sái Võng
prov_r1_17.lore: Wide pine forest and lake shore whose fishers hang their nets to dry on frames along every path. A small cold lake lies inland among the trees. The province sends fish and net cord to Quy Điểu Trấn and to Hàm Nguyệt Trang's pearl beds.

prov_r1_18.name: Liệp Hộ
prov_r1_18.lore: Higher inland forest of spruce and pine where hunters' families trap marten, fox and deer. A green-canopied spirit vein of wood qi lies under the ridge. Furs from here are sold at the winter ice market of Quy Điểu.

prov_r1_19.name: Phóng Phiệt
prov_r1_19.lore: Forest on a river near the long lake, where loggers bind dead and windfallen trunks into rafts and float them down. A quiet pool by the river hides its own small pearl bed. Tùng Đào's foresters mark every raft before it leaves.

prov_r1_2.name: Bạch Mang Hoang
prov_r1_2.lore: Bare tundra on the northern shore, white for nine months of the year. No one lives here; the cold wind off the water keeps even herders away. A spirit vein of water qi lies frozen in a hollow near its middle, and Tùng Đào's cultivators come to it in summer.

prov_r1_20.name: Tịch Ba
prov_r1_20.lore: Shore forest whose fishers go out when the evening waves calm. Its people fish, cut ice in winter and hunt lynx in the woods behind. On the shore lie the broken walls of Nghênh Nguyệt Trấn, crushed by the ice shove of 1033.

prov_r1_21.name: Tạc Băng
prov_r1_21.lore: Pine and cedar forest on the shore near Hàn Yên and Noãn Ốc. Its people cut blocks of lake ice in winter and pack them in sawdust to keep fish through the summer. Tùng Đào's stewards buy the ice for the granaries of the north.

prov_r1_22.name: Tùng Kiều
prov_r1_22.lore: Upland pine forest on a river, crossed by a long bridge of whole pine trunks. Woodsmen and pine-nut gatherers live here, and the wood above the river is a favourite place for listening to the pines. Tùng Đào has let Sương Tùng Các build its pavilion in the higher woods.

prov_r1_23.name: Thạch Than
prov_r1_23.lore: Inland spruce forest along a stony river. Its people fish the shallows, gather spruce gum and float small loads of wood downstream. The river is too shallow for boats above the village, so goods go on by mule.

prov_r1_24.name: Hồ Khẩu
prov_r1_24.lore: Forest where a river opens into the long lake, rich with fish and reeds. Hồ Khẩu Thôn lives by fishing and by the boats that pass in and out of the river. Its red pine woods give the best mast timber in the north.

prov_r1_25.name: Tùng Tử
prov_r1_25.lore: Rolling forest of old pines whose people live by gathering pine nuts each autumn. An ancient spirit vein of wood qi lies under a single huge tree. Pine-nut oil from here is pressed for lamps all over the north.

prov_r1_26.name: Sơn Ổ
prov_r1_26.lore: The first real hills of the southern forest, climbing above five hundred metres. Villagers gather mushrooms and wild honey in the hollows and keep a few goats. The ruin of Tà Dương Trấn on the slope warns them not to build where the hillside is soft.

prov_r1_27.name: Hệ Bì
prov_r1_27.lore: Forest on a river at the edge of Phản Cảnh Lâm. Its people are woodcutters and guides who tie bark strips to the trees so the lost can follow the light out of the forest. Tùng Đào's patrols rest here before skirting the forest edge.

prov_r1_28.name: Song Thụ
prov_r1_28.lore: Deep river forest of mixed pine and birch. Its villagers fish and gather herbs, and tend the overgrown terraces of the fallen Lãnh Hương Viện for the cold-flower incense herbs that still grow there. Tùng Đào took the old academy's disciples in when it fell.

prov_r1_29.name: Phong Khẩu
prov_r1_29.lore: High forested hills at the region's southern edge, cut by a windy gap where the old post road once ran. Its people keep goats and gather pine nuts, and brown bears hold the crags above. The empty post town on the gap fell out of use when the road moved.

prov_r1_3.name: Đống Thổ Nguyên
prov_r1_3.lore: Flat, frozen tundra on the northern shore, wet in the short summer and iron-hard in winter. No one lives here. A deep vein of water qi lies under the frost, and it never thaws.

prov_r1_4.name: Tàn Tuyết Câu
prov_r1_4.lore: Tundra and stunted forest in shallow gullies where snow lies until midsummer. No one lives here now, though the stones of the old Bắc Minh Quán still stand on the shore. A cold spring of water qi runs from the gullies.

prov_r1_5.name: Thương Mang Nguyên
prov_r1_5.lore: Grey tundra and thin larch woods stretching to the northern shore. Only herders in summer cross it. A vein of frost-bound water qi lies under a low rise, and Tùng Đào's disciples come to temper themselves in its cold.

prov_r1_6.name: Mục Lộc
prov_r1_6.lore: Inland forest giving way to tundra in the north, where reindeer families of the same stock as Tuyết Lộc's herders keep their winter grounds. They trade hides, antler and smoked meat south. The forest is bowed under snow for half the year.

prov_r1_7.name: Bắc Ngạn
prov_r1_7.lore: A broad forest running up to the cold northern shore. Its people hunt seals on the ice and fish through holes in winter, and cut timber in summer. Giant boars root in the inland woods, and villagers fence their stores against them.

prov_r1_8.name: Băng Võng
prov_r1_8.lore: Forest, bog and tundra on the northern shore, where fishers set long nets under the ice. Golden eagles nest on a rock table inland and take hares and young deer. Its people pay Tùng Đào in dried fish and eagle feathers.

prov_r1_9.name: Ô Nê Trạch
prov_r1_9.lore: A cold black-mud marsh on the shore, frozen half the year and stinking in summer. No one lives here; the poison toads of its shoals are reason enough. Alchemists' collectors come for toad venom in late summer.

prov_ham_nguyet_lake_1.name: Trầm Bích Đàm
prov_ham_nguyet_lake_1.gloss: Pool of the Sunken Jade Disc
prov_ham_nguyet_lake_1.look: A round, still side lake behind a sand bar off the long lake, ringed by birches, so calm that the full moon lies in it like a jade disc dropped to the bottom.
prov_ham_nguyet_lake_1.lore: The sand bar closed this bay off from Hạo Nguyệt Hồ long ago, and Hàm Nguyệt Trang's novices practise here before they are let near the Moon Net. Its water is cold and deep, and pearl mussels grow slowly in it.

prov_ham_nguyet_ruin_2.name: Cựu Châu Trấn
prov_ham_nguyet_ruin_2.look: Low stone footings and the stumps of pier posts on a bare shore, half buried in sand and birch saplings, with heaps of old mussel shells grown over by moss.
prov_ham_nguyet_ruin_2.lore: Pearl farmers built this town soon after the great pearl of 470 was found. When the lake froze to its bed in 748, the town's pearl beds died, and by the next year its people had moved to Hàm Nguyệt Trang's shore.

prov_p55_forest_1.name: Bách Điểu Lâm
prov_p55_forest_1.look: A low pine and birch wood behind Quy Điểu Trấn whose every branch is crowded with birds in autumn, the ground white with droppings and feathers.
prov_p55_forest_1.lore: The homing flocks rest here before settling on the town's nest poles. Fowlers take only what the town allows, and a feather-gatherer who robs a nest is fined a pearl.

prov_p95_beast_lair_1.name: Tuyết Báo Cương
prov_p95_beast_lair_1.look: A low wooded knoll above the bogs, its rocks scored with claw marks and the snow around it trampled into tracks that lead nowhere near the village.
prov_p95_beast_lair_1.lore: Snow leopards den among its rocks, kin, the herders say, to the spirit beast Hàm Nguyệt Trang hunted across the ice in 610. Herders keep their reindeer well away from it.

prov_p96_spirit_vein_1.name: Ngưng Yên Nhãn
prov_p96_spirit_vein_1.look: A small round hollow in the pines behind Hàn Yên Thôn, where a thin column of mist rises and hangs frozen in the air on still winter days.
prov_p96_spirit_vein_1.lore: A small spirit vein of Water qi, cold and clear, wells up here; villagers say it is why the village smoke freezes. Hàm Nguyệt Trang's disciples come to sit in its mist.

prov_p97_spirit_vein_1.name: Ôn Thủy Mạch
prov_p97_spirit_vein_1.look: A line of snow-free ground runs through the pines behind Noãn Ốc Thôn, steaming faintly, with green moss even in midwinter.
prov_p97_spirit_vein_1.lore: A spirit vein of Water qi runs here with a faint warmth in it, and it feeds the hot spring found under the snow in 1015. Old cultivators who soak at Noãn Ốc say the vein, not the spring, is what eases their bones.

prov_r1_1_beast_lair_1.name: Bạch Hùng Nguyên
prov_r1_1_beast_lair_1.look: Flat white tundra near the shore, pocked with snow dens and old seal bones, where great white shapes rise and lie down again in the wind.
prov_r1_1_beast_lair_1.lore: White bears come ashore here each autumn and den through the winter. Herders cross the plain only in midsummer, when the bears are out on the water.

prov_r1_10_beast_lair_1.name: Quần Lang Lâm
prov_r1_10_beast_lair_1.look: A dark fir wood on low wet ground, its trails beaten hard by many paws, with gnawed antlers scattered under the trees.
prov_r1_10_beast_lair_1.lore: Several wolf packs share this wood and fight over it in winter, and their howling carries to the tundra. Trappers take pelts from its edge and never camp inside.

prov_r1_11_village_1.name: Tùng Chi Thôn
prov_r1_11_village_1.look: Log houses among old pines, each trunk scarred with neat V-shaped cuts above a clay cup, and pitch kettles smoking in the yard.
prov_r1_11_village_1.lore: The village taps resin and boils it into pitch for the lake boats, cutting no living tree. Its pitch-makers say the best resin comes from trees older than Tùng Đào Cung.

prov_r1_11_spirit_vein_2.name: Lão Căn Mạch
prov_r1_11_spirit_vein_2.look: On a rise in the forest, a tangle of huge exposed pine roots arches over bare ground that hums faintly when pressed with a palm.
prov_r1_11_spirit_vein_2.lore: A spirit vein of Wood qi runs under the roots of the oldest pines here. Resin from these trees is said to stay soft for a hundred years.

prov_r1_11_ruin_3.name: Điêu Bì Trấn
prov_r1_11_ruin_3.look: On a wooded hill, the log walls of a small town have fallen inward, and rusted traps still hang on pegs inside the roofless fur store.
prov_r1_11_ruin_3.lore: Fur traders built Điêu Bì Trấn when sable fur was worth its weight in silver. By 1020 the sables were trapped out of the hills, and within two years the last traders left for the lake towns.

prov_r1_12_village_1.name: Ngư Đăng Thôn
prov_r1_12_village_1.look: A shore village of low grey roofs where dozens of boat lanterns hang from poles along the beach, lit together on autumn nights.
prov_r1_12_village_1.lore: Its fishers draw fish to their nets with lantern light in autumn, and from the far shore the boats look like a second string of stars. They sell their smoked catch at Quy Điểu.

prov_r1_12_beast_lair_2.name: Dạ Kiêu Lâm
prov_r1_12_beast_lair_2.look: A swampy pine wood where pellets of fur and bone lie thick under hollow trees, and at dusk great pale owls drift between the trunks.
prov_r1_12_beast_lair_2.lore: Owls as big as children nest in its hollow trees and hunt the swamp edge at night. Villagers say an owl that follows a boat home means a death in the house.

prov_r1_13_village_1.name: Tùng Than Thôn
prov_r1_13_village_1.look: Grey-roofed houses along a pale beach under tall pines, boats drawn up on log rollers and pitch pots smoking by the water.
prov_r1_13_village_1.lore: Its people build small boats from windfallen pine and caulk them with their own pitch. Lake fishers from all along the shore come here to buy a hull.

prov_r1_13_forest_2.name: Vạn Tùng Lâm
prov_r1_13_forest_2.look: An endless stand of straight red-brown pines on gentle ground, so even that the trunks seem to repeat to the edge of sight.
prov_r1_13_forest_2.lore: Tùng Đào's surveyors once tried to count its trees and stopped at ten thousand, which gave the forest its name. Woodsmen get lost in it because every view looks the same.

prov_r1_14_village_1.name: Hồi Lưu Thôn
prov_r1_14_village_1.look: Stilt houses stand over a still backwater where the river meets the shore, wicker eel traps stacked on every porch.
prov_r1_14_village_1.lore: The villagers trap eels in the river's backwaters and smoke them over birch. Hàm Nguyệt Trang takes its dues in eel each autumn and serves them at its moon feast.

prov_r1_14_forest_2.name: Tố Hoa Lâm
prov_r1_14_forest_2.look: A pale, quiet birch wood on flat ground, its white trunks peeling in long curls and the floor carpeted with yellow leaves.
prov_r1_14_forest_2.lore: The villages strip bark here for boxes and writing sheets, never more than one strip from a tree in a year. Hàm Nguyệt Trang's records are kept on its bark.

prov_r1_15_village_1.name: Thán Diêu Thôn
prov_r1_15_village_1.look: A clearing ringed by earth-covered charcoal mounds, smoking day and night, with soot-black houses and stacks of deadwood.
prov_r1_15_village_1.lore: The burners make charcoal only from dead and fallen wood, as Tùng Đào requires, and haul it to the lake towns before the snow. Their children are black to the elbows by the age of five.

prov_r1_15_forest_2.name: Lạc Diệp Lâm
prov_r1_15_forest_2.look: A larch forest that turns gold in autumn and drops every needle, leaving the trunks bare and the ground soft and bright.
prov_r1_15_forest_2.lore: Larch is the one conifer here that sheds its needles, and the burners gather the fallen wood for their kilns. In winter the bare forest is the easiest place in the north to track game.

prov_r1_16_town_1.name: Nguyệt Tân Trấn
prov_r1_16_town_1.look: A timber-walled town on the river bank, its ferry stair running into the water beside rows of pitch-black barges.
prov_r1_16_town_1.lore: Nguyệt Tân Trấn ferries timber, pitch and pearls between the long lake and the inland villages. Its ferry runs only by moonlight in the busy season, so the day stays free for loading.

prov_r1_16_lake_2.name: Tẩy Nguyệt Đàm
prov_r1_16_lake_2.look: A small, clear lake in the pines near the river, its pebble bed visible far out from the shore.
prov_r1_16_lake_2.lore: Fishers say the moon comes down to wash here before it rises over the long lake. Hàm Nguyệt Trang's disciples once kept spirit fish in it, and a few still swim there.

prov_r1_17_village_1.name: Sái Võng Thôn
prov_r1_17_village_1.look: Every path in this forest village is lined with tall frames of drying nets, so walking through it is like walking through a maze of grey lace.
prov_r1_17_village_1.lore: Its people twist net cord from nettle and birch bast and sell nets to fishers all along the lake. A net from Sái Võng is said to last ten winters.

prov_r1_17_lake_2.name: Hàn Kính Hồ
prov_r1_17_lake_2.look: A dark, round forest lake that freezes clear as glass in winter, the trees and sky reflected perfectly in its ice.
prov_r1_17_lake_2.lore: Its ice is so clear that the fish can be seen moving under it. Young cultivators of Hàm Nguyệt Trang come to sit on the ice and still their minds.

prov_r1_18_village_1.name: Liệp Hộ Thôn
prov_r1_18_village_1.look: A cluster of log houses with racks of stretched pelts, antlers nailed over every door and hounds sleeping in the snow.
prov_r1_18_village_1.lore: Its families have trapped marten, fox and deer here for generations and sell their furs at the winter ice market. Every hunter swears never to take a beast's young.

prov_r1_18_spirit_vein_2.name: Thúy Cái Mạch
prov_r1_18_spirit_vein_2.look: On a forested ridge, a ring of spruces with unusually dense, deep-green crowns closes overhead like a roof, and the ground beneath stays dry in any rain.
prov_r1_18_spirit_vein_2.lore: A spirit vein of Wood qi rises under the ridge and feeds the spruces above it. Tùng Đào's wardens visit it each spring and keep the hunters from camping inside the ring.

prov_r1_19_village_1.name: Phóng Phiệt Thôn
prov_r1_19_village_1.look: On a river bank, bound log rafts lie in rows on the mud, each branded with the pine mark of Tùng Đào's foresters.
prov_r1_19_village_1.lore: The villagers float windfallen and dead trunks down to the lake towns in spring flood. No raft leaves without a forester's brand, and a raft without one is burned.

prov_r1_19_lake_2.name: Tàng Châu Đàm
prov_r1_19_lake_2.look: A deep, reed-fringed pool beside the river, its dark water ringed with white mussel shells on the shore.
prov_r1_19_lake_2.lore: A small bed of pearl mussels lives here, hidden from the Băng Tâm skiffs during the Long Lake War. Hàm Nguyệt Trang now keeps it as seed stock for its beds.

prov_r1_2_spirit_vein_1.name: Hàn Lộ Huyệt
prov_r1_2_spirit_vein_1.look: A shallow hollow in the tundra where frost forms on every blade of lichen even at midsummer noon, and the air smells of snow.
prov_r1_2_spirit_vein_1.lore: A spirit vein of Water qi surfaces here, cold enough to freeze dew on a summer day. Tùng Đào's water cultivators come in the short summer, when the walk is possible.

prov_r1_20_village_1.name: Tịch Ba Thôn
prov_r1_20_village_1.look: A row of grey-roofed houses facing the water, boats pulled up at the tide line and nets set out on poles in the evening calm.
prov_r1_20_village_1.lore: Its fishers go out only when the evening waves settle, a habit learned after the ice shove that crushed Nghênh Nguyệt Trấn. They sell their catch and winter ice at Quy Điểu.

prov_r1_20_beast_lair_2.name: Sơn Miêu Cương
prov_r1_20_beast_lair_2.look: A rocky knoll in thick pine, its boulders scratched and its snow marked by broad, furred tracks.
prov_r1_20_beast_lair_2.lore: Lynxes den among its boulders and hunt hares through the forest. Villagers say a lynx can see through a wall, and hang their meat high.

prov_r1_20_ruin_3.name: Nghênh Nguyệt Trấn
prov_r1_20_ruin_3.look: On the shore, the stone walls of a town lean inland, pushed over in long rows, with heaps of boulders shoved up among the house footings.
prov_r1_20_ruin_3.lore: The town greeted the moonrise over the water from its harbour wall for six centuries. In the spring of 1033 a storm drove the breaking ice ashore in a wall, flattening the harbour and half the town, and its people never rebuilt.

prov_r1_21_village_1.name: Tạc Băng Thôn
prov_r1_21_village_1.look: A shore village where great blocks of ice lie stacked under sawdust in long sheds, and saws and ice picks hang on every wall.
prov_r1_21_village_1.lore: In winter its people saw ice from the frozen shore and pack it in sawdust to keep fish all summer. Tùng Đào's stewards buy ice for the northern granaries.

prov_r1_21_forest_2.name: Tuyết Tùng Lâm
prov_r1_21_forest_2.look: A wood of broad cedars with layered branches that hold the snow in flat white shelves.
prov_r1_21_forest_2.lore: Its cedar is fragrant and resists rot, and the lake villages build their shrines from it. Only a fallen cedar may be taken, by Tùng Đào's rule.

prov_r1_22_village_1.name: Tùng Kiều Thôn
prov_r1_22_village_1.look: A village on both banks of a river, joined by a long bridge of whole pine trunks pinned with wooden pegs.
prov_r1_22_village_1.lore: The bridge was built from pines felled by one storm, and each family mends its own trunk. Pilgrims cross it on their way up to the listening wood.

prov_r1_22_forest_2.name: Thính Tùng Lâm
prov_r1_22_forest_2.gloss: Wood Where One Listens to the Pines
prov_r1_22_forest_2.look: An upland pine wood where flat stones have been set among the trunks as seats, and the wind in the crowns sounds like distant surf.
prov_r1_22_forest_2.lore: Tùng Đào's disciples of the north come here to hear the pine waves when they cannot travel to the seat. The stones are said to have been set by the first steward of the north.

prov_r1_22_minor_seat_p.name: Sương Tùng Các
prov_r1_22_minor_seat_p.look: A three-roofed pavilion of dark pine stands on a frosty rise among old trees, and from every branch around it hang small paper lanterns painted with talismans.
prov_r1_22_minor_seat_p.lore: Sương Tùng Các is a small sect of talisman makers sworn to Tùng Đào Cung, who write their talismans on paper made from birch bark and pine resin. Its ward lanterns hang in the lake villages to keep beasts and frost spirits off the doors in winter.

sect.name: Sương Tùng Các
sect.craft: talismans (phù lục) on pine-resin paper; ward lanterns

prov_r1_23_village_1.name: Thạch Than Thôn
prov_r1_23_village_1.look: Grey-roofed houses above a wide, stony river where children wade the shallows with spears and mules wait on the bank.
prov_r1_23_village_1.lore: The river is too shallow for boats above the village, so goods come and go by mule. Its people spear fish in the shallows and gather spruce gum.

prov_r1_23_forest_2.name: Vân Sam Lâm
prov_r1_23_forest_2.look: A dark, dense spruce forest whose tall spires vanish into low cloud on grey days.
prov_r1_23_forest_2.lore: Spruce from here is light and strong and goes to make zither soundboards in the pine sea. Gum gatherers work its edge in summer.

prov_r1_24_village_1.name: Hồ Khẩu Thôn
prov_r1_24_village_1.look: A village of grey roofs where a river opens into the long lake, its jetties busy with fishing boats and timber barges.
prov_r1_24_village_1.lore: Every boat going up the river passes Hồ Khẩu, and the village lives by fish, reeds and the boatmen's custom. Tùng Đào keeps a toll post on its jetty.

prov_r1_24_forest_2.name: Hồng Tùng Lâm
prov_r1_24_forest_2.look: A wood of tall, straight pines with reddish bark, their crowns far above a clear floor.
prov_r1_24_forest_2.lore: These red pines give the best mast timber in the north, and only windfalls may be taken. Shipwrights from the lake towns come to choose their trunks in person.

prov_r1_25_village_1.name: Tùng Tử Thôn
prov_r1_25_village_1.look: A hill village where pine cones lie drying in heaps on every roof and the smell of roasted nuts hangs in the air.
prov_r1_25_village_1.lore: Its people live by gathering pine nuts each autumn and pressing them for lamp oil. They leave one cone in ten for the squirrels, saying the squirrels plant the next forest.

prov_r1_25_spirit_vein_2.name: Cổ Mộc Nhãn
prov_r1_25_spirit_vein_2.look: In a clearing stands a single colossal pine, its trunk hollow at the base, and inside the hollow the air shimmers faintly green.
prov_r1_25_spirit_vein_2.lore: A spirit vein of Wood qi comes to the surface inside the old pine's hollow. Tùng Đào allows one disciple at a time to sit in it, for a month at most.

prov_r1_26_village_1.name: Sơn Ổ Thôn
prov_r1_26_village_1.look: Houses tucked into a sheltered hollow in the hills, log beehives on the slope and baskets of mushrooms drying on the eaves.
prov_r1_26_village_1.lore: Its people gather mushrooms and wild honey and keep a few goats. They remember Tà Dương Trấn and build only on rock.

prov_r1_26_forest_2.name: Bàn Căn Lâm
prov_r1_26_forest_2.look: On a steep hillside, pines grow from bare rock, their roots coiling over the stones like ropes.
prov_r1_26_forest_2.lore: The roots hold the slope together, and the villages forbid cutting here. After Tà Dương Trấn slid away, no one argues with the rule.

prov_r1_26_ruin_3.name: Tà Dương Trấn
prov_r1_26_ruin_3.look: A raw scar of earth runs down a hillside, and at its foot the timbers and roofs of a small town lie broken in a heap of mud and stones grown over with birch.
prov_r1_26_ruin_3.lore: A hill town of honey and timber traders, built on a sunny western slope. In the long rains of 1104 the hillside slid away and buried half the town in a night, and the rest was left.

prov_r1_27_village_1.name: Hệ Bì Thôn
prov_r1_27_village_1.look: A river village at the edge of Phản Cảnh Lâm, where bundles of birch bark strips hang by every door, ready to be tied to trees.
prov_r1_27_village_1.lore: Its woodcutters and guides tie bark strips on the ways into Phản Cảnh Lâm so the lost can follow the light out. Tùng Đào's patrols rest here and ask the guides what they have seen.

prov_r1_28_village_1.name: Song Thụ Thôn
prov_r1_28_village_1.look: A river village gathered around two huge pines that grew from one root, their trunks splitting apart above the roofs.
prov_r1_28_village_1.lore: Villagers fish the river and gather incense herbs from the old terraces of Lãnh Hương Viện. Couples are married under the twin pines.

prov_r1_28_forest_2.name: U Thúy Lâm
prov_r1_28_forest_2.look: A deep wood of pine and fir where moss covers every stone and fallen log in a thick green fleece.
prov_r1_28_forest_2.lore: The forest is so damp and quiet that herb gatherers find mosses here that grow nowhere else. Its paths lead up to the old academy's terraces.

prov_r1_28_ruin_3.name: Lãnh Hương Viện
prov_r1_28_ruin_3.look: On a wooded rise, terraces of overgrown herb beds climb to the roofless halls of an academy, its incense burners still standing in the moss.
prov_r1_28_ruin_3.lore: A small sect of incense makers who burned cold-flower herbs to calm the mind in cultivation. Its last master died in seclusion in 890 with no heir named, and Tùng Đào took in its disciples; its herbs still grow on the terraces.

prov_r1_29_village_1.name: Phong Khẩu Thôn
prov_r1_29_village_1.look: Low stone-walled houses huddle in a windy gap in the hills, roofs weighted with rocks, goats sheltering in the lee.
prov_r1_29_village_1.lore: The wind through the gap never stops, and its people keep goats and gather pine nuts. They still keep the old post road's well, though few travellers come.

prov_r1_29_beast_lair_2.name: Tông Hùng Nhai
prov_r1_29_beast_lair_2.look: A forested crag above the gap, its caves marked by stripped bark and claw-torn stumps.
prov_r1_29_beast_lair_2.lore: Brown bears den in its caves through the winter and raid the beehives below in spring. The villagers leave a pot of honey at the foot of the crag each autumn, hoping to be left alone.

prov_r1_29_ruin_3.name: Dịch Lộ Trấn
prov_r1_29_ruin_3.look: High on a hill, the stone stables and inn walls of a post town stand roofless beside a paved road that runs into the forest and vanishes.
prov_r1_29_ruin_3.lore: Tùng Đào built the post town when it took Lãnh Nguyệt Lâm, on the hill road from the pine sea. When the lake road along the water was finished, the hill road was abandoned, and the town emptied by 868.

prov_r1_3_spirit_vein_1.name: Vĩnh Đống Huyệt
prov_r1_3_spirit_vein_1.look: A sunken pit in the tundra lined with blue ice that never thaws, breathing cold mist even in summer.
prov_r1_3_spirit_vein_1.lore: A spirit vein of Water qi runs here so cold that the ground has not thawed in living memory. Tùng Đào's disciples who cultivate in it wrap themselves in fur and stay a day at most.

prov_r1_4_spirit_vein_1.name: Bạch Dạ Tuyền
prov_r1_4_spirit_vein_1.look: A cold spring wells up among stunted larches and runs in a clear thread over the tundra, catching the low light of the summer nights.
prov_r1_4_spirit_vein_1.lore: A spirit vein of Water qi feeds this spring, strongest in the white nights of midsummer. The hermits of Bắc Minh Quán drank only from it.

prov_r1_4_ruin_2.name: Bắc Minh Quán
prov_r1_4_ruin_2.look: On a bare shore, a ring of low stone cells stands around a fallen hall, its doorways facing the northern water.
prov_r1_4_ruin_2.lore: Hermits of water arts built this abbey to watch the northern water through the long dark. They never took more than a handful of disciples, and when Tùng Đào came north in 330 the last of them went to the palace and left the abbey empty.

prov_r1_5_spirit_vein_1.name: Ngưng Sương Mạch
prov_r1_5_spirit_vein_1.look: A low rise in the tundra is crusted with thick white frost in a long line, as though a frozen river ran just under the lichen.
prov_r1_5_spirit_vein_1.lore: A spirit vein of Water qi runs under the rise and draws frost out of the air. Tùng Đào's disciples come to temper their bodies in its cold.

prov_r1_6_village_1.name: Mục Lộc Thôn
prov_r1_6_village_1.look: Log houses and hide tents at the forest edge, reindeer corralled behind fences of split pine and antlers piled by the doors.
prov_r1_6_village_1.lore: Its herders are cousins of Tuyết Lộc's and keep their winter grounds here. They trade hides, antler and smoked meat south to the lake towns.

prov_r1_6_forest_2.name: Tuyết Áp Lâm
prov_r1_6_forest_2.look: A pine forest whose young trees are bent into arches under heavy snow, making tunnels across the paths.
prov_r1_6_forest_2.lore: Snow lies so heavy here that the trees grow crooked, and the herders drive their reindeer through the arches. Bent pine from here makes the best sled runners.

prov_r1_7_village_1.name: Bắc Ngạn Thôn
prov_r1_7_village_1.look: Grey-roofed log houses on the cold northern shore, sleds and harpoons stacked by the doors and seal hides stretched on frames.
prov_r1_7_village_1.lore: Its people hunt seals on the ice and fish through holes in winter. Seal oil from here lights the lamps of the northern villages.

prov_r1_7_beast_lair_2.name: Cự Thỉ Cương
prov_r1_7_beast_lair_2.look: A knoll in the forest torn up as if ploughed, with trees rubbed bare at shoulder height and wallows of black mud.
prov_r1_7_beast_lair_2.lore: Boars the size of oxen root here and raid the village stores in lean winters. Hunters go after them only in groups of ten.

prov_r1_8_village_1.name: Băng Võng Thôn
prov_r1_8_village_1.look: A shore village where long lines of holes cut through the ice lead out from the beach, each with a net cord frozen to a stake.
prov_r1_8_village_1.lore: Its fishers feed long nets under the ice from hole to hole and haul them at dawn. They pay Tùng Đào in dried fish and eagle feathers.

prov_r1_8_beast_lair_2.name: Kim Điêu Đài
prov_r1_8_beast_lair_2.look: A flat-topped rock rises out of the forest, its edges heaped with great stick nests and the bones of hares and fawns.
prov_r1_8_beast_lair_2.lore: Golden eagles nest on the rock and hunt the forest and tundra for miles. Their fallen feathers are prized by fletchers, and villagers gather them under the cliff.

prov_r1_9_beast_lair_1.name: Độc Thiềm Chử
prov_r1_9_beast_lair_1.look: Low mud shoals in a black marsh, their surface covered in warty toads the size of a man's head, croaking in a deep drone.
prov_r1_9_beast_lair_1.lore: Poison toads breed on the shoals in summer, and their venom blisters the skin. Alchemists' collectors come in late summer with gloves and jars.
